rules.rule: Check for urgent low mood, stress or anxiety conditions
Check for generalised anxiety disorder and PTSD features
rules.problem: Type, trigger and coverage are right (every red-box item and every discriminating finding for both 'likely' diagnoses is listed). Minor: Distress stands in for 'impaired function/distress' (c010).

rules.rule: Diagnose probable generalised anxiety disorder (low mood, stress or anxiety page)
rules.problem: Distress is a hard AND conjunct although the page gives it as one of two alternatives ('impaired function/distress'); patients with functionally impairing worry but no recorded distress are excluded. The 6-month onset test and the >=3-of-6 expansion (4 or-branches with any2) are correct and 'likely' -> probable is right.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable post-traumatic stress disorder (low mood, stress or anxiety page)
rules.problem: Structure matches the page: anxiety onset >= 1 month, bad experience, >=3 of 4 groups (nightmares/flashbacks, avoidance, on guard/startled, numb/detached) correctly expanded with nested or. 'likely' -> probable is right.

rules.rule: Urgent: low mood, stress or anxiety with suicidal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: Red box 'Give urgent attention' justifies Urgent; (and presenting-complaint (or red-box items)) follows the house pattern.

summary: Nothing invented: every condition traces to the page and all 24 SNOMED concepts exist. The one real distortion is in the GAD rule, where Distress is required as a hard conjunct although the page offers 'impaired function/distress' as alternatives, so the rule is narrower than the page. Not encoded (no 'likely' wording, so low severity): the phobia/panic line ('discuss/refer'; Phobia and Panic attack findings exist for a possible rule), the depression screen (-> 159), the substance-use screen (-> 165) and 'if known with depression -> 160', all of which are routing rather than diagnosis.
